newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: MTIA says wage case outcome reasonable.
newsitem.headline: MTIA says wage case outcome reasonable.

text.p: Australian employer group, the Metal Trades Industry Association of Australia (MTIA), said on Tuesday a A$10 a week pay rise awarded to lower paid workers was a "reasonable outcome" to the latest wage case.
Chief executive Bob Herbert said the MTIA had argued for an A$8 a week rise, but was pleased the increase could be absorbed into over-award payments.
"This will mean that for the great majority of employers in the manufacturing and construction industry, the impact of the decision will be negligible," he said.

Australia's Industrial Relations Commission (AIRC) earlier granted lower paid workers a A$10 a week pay rise and rejected the Australian Council of Trade Union's (ACTU) claim for an 8.75 percent pay rise across the board.
The AIRC also set a A$359.40 per week minimum wage, which was below the ACTU's claim for a A$380 a week minimum wage.
